notes.auth: Native OIDC: anansi has its own accounts + per-user data, so only it can map a Pocket ID identity onto the right rows. The platform provides the client (id `anansi`, secret from clients.sops) and the OIDC_* env; the app repo owns the Auth.js provider.

env.note: ON: probe cameras live so cards show current frames instead of the static Shodan still. This dials arbitrary exposed cameras straight from the house's IP — enabled deliberately.
Write successful live frames back into the screenshot store, so the cached still stays fresh for when probing is off/unreachable.
Cams pulled per Shodan query. ~1 credit / 100 results / query, so this is the main lever on credit burn. Upstream prod runs 2999.
Maintenance brake, held off. "true" 503s the APIs and redirects HTML to /offline-for-now.

OFF: the Shodan pull runs on a Nitro in-process cron (daily 00:00), not at boot. On-boot refresh only fires when the DB is empty, but keeping it off means a fresh install waits for the cron or a manual trigger rather than pulling during first boot.
The app reads its own canonical origin from this, not from the APP_PUBLIC_URL the apps module injects.

notes.app: Fork of github.com/alectrocute/ipcrawl (MIT), rebranded to Argus and since migrated to TanStack Start; upstream still runs the public ipcrawl.com, which is why that name survives in the UI's attribution and nowhere else. Upstream has no Dockerfile and deploys as systemd+nginx on a VPS; the fork adds the Dockerfile + .github/workflows/image.yml, and CI derives the image name from the GitHub repo name, so `image` and `hostname` are both left null and derived from this key. Rebase the fork on upstream to pick up changes.
notes.auth: Forward-auth: Argus has no user model, so the gate belongs in front of it rather than inside it. No app-side change, and no identity headers — nothing downstream would read them. /favicon.ico is the health path and therefore the primary bypass: harmless unauthenticated, and it comes from the app itself, so gatus and the deploy check certify the upstream instead of the middleware's 302. bypassRule adds the three icon paths for the same reason daedalus needs them — a gated /icon.svg answers the IdP's HTML, so the app list would show a monogram instead of the mark (and iOS a letter tile instead of the home-screen icon).
notes.stage: LAN-only. This is a catalogue of other people's exposed webcams; publishing it on a CNAME under our own domain is a decision to make deliberately, not a default.
notes.egress: All outbound (camera live-probes + the daily Shodan pull) exits through the dedicated ProtonVPN tunnel in stacks/argus-vpn/ instead of the house WAN IP. The app leaves traefik-net and rides gluetun-argus's netns; traefik reaches the UI via the host port gluetun publishes.
notes.secrets: SHODAN_API_KEY + VOTER_PEPPER + CAM_ID_PEPPER come from the tracked stacks/apps/argus-env.sops (operatorSecrets). Without a Shodan key the app still boots and serves; the catalogue is just empty. The machine-generated secrets/argus/env keeps only the bootstrap AUTH_SECRET.
notes.storage: The catalogue is in the shared pg cluster (migrated off SQLite 2026-08-08); the `storage` bind mount now holds only camera stills and a few fs-backed status records, joined to rows by cams.id + cams.screenshot_mime. Schema is applied by Drizzle migrations at container start (start.mjs), which exits non-zero rather than serving against a schema that doesn't match the code. Because this app rides gluetun's netns it has no bridge to reach `pg` on, so its DATABASE_URL points at the cluster's plain-TCP host port — see appDatabases.argus.reach, derived from `egress`.
